At the interim stage to this proceeding, the Freight Forwarders Institute submitted a report prepared by a research and consulting firm entitled, "An Assessment of the Population-Mileage Formula," This study consisted largely of an analysis of data on population and employment with respect to 12 major cities. Much of these data were reproduced in the Interim Report (see <u>Commercial Zones</u>, 124 M.C.C. at 159-160 and 199-201). On the basis of that information the consulting firm reached the following conclusions:
(1) Major cities are experiencing an accelerating tendency to expand outward. The growth rate for the area surrounding the selected central cities has been more than five times that of the central cities.
(2) Decentralization of metropolitan areas is also apparent from an employment standpoint. The SMSA employment figures for the 12 studied cities reveal that the central cities' share of overall SMSA employment in manufacturing, retail and wholesale trade, and selected services declined when compared to the surrounding area.
(3) Present commercial zone and terminal area imits are outdated, since they include a diminishing share of urban population.
